title: Keep CI tool versions up to date with the GitLab Renovate bot
description:
## Summary

Every tool version used by the chart's CI pipeline is pinned by hand in `.gitlab-ci.yml` (`ALPINE_IMAGE_TAG`, `DOCKER_VERSION`, `HELM_VERSION`, `HELM_UNITTEST_PLUGIN_VERSION`, `KIND_VERSION`, `KUBECTL_VERSION`). The last bump before #602 was !421 in August 2023, after which several of them went end-of-life unnoticed.

## Proposal

Onboard this project to the GitLab Renovate bot, https://gitlab.com/orbit/frontend/renovate-gitlab-bot, the same way `orbit/orbit`, `orbit/gl-openshift/orbit-operator` and `orbit/team/gitlab` are handled. The bot then opens an MR whenever one of these tools publishes a new release.

Following the bot's [setup process](https://gitlab.com/orbit/frontend/renovate-gitlab-bot/-/blob/main/docs/setting-up-a-new-project.md), this needs two MRs in the bot repository:

1. Add `{ path = "orbit/team/orbit", fork_path = "charts-gitlab-runner" }` to `forks/config.tfvars` (the bot maintains a mirror fork under `gitlab-renovate-forks`).
2. Add `renovate/projects/charts-gitlab-runner.config.js` with a `custom.regex` manager per CI variable:
   - `ALPINE_IMAGE_TAG` → docker `alpine`
   - `DOCKER_VERSION` → docker `docker`
   - `HELM_VERSION` → docker `alpine/helm`
   - `HELM_UNITTEST_PLUGIN_VERSION` → github-releases `helm-unittest/helm-unittest`
   - `KIND_VERSION` → github-releases `kubernetes-sigs/kind`
   - `KUBECTL_VERSION` → github-tags `kubernetes/kubernetes`

   with `kind` and `kubectl` grouped into one MR, default labels (`maintenance::dependency`, `type::maintenance`), reviewers from the `runner-helm` roulette project and `semanticCommits: "disabled"`.

## Notes

- The Renovate fork has no `AUTHENTICATION_TOKEN`, so the `integration test *` jobs cannot run there. Reviewers have to run the MR pipeline from the canonical project; the MR template note should say so, as `charts/gitlab` does.
- Depends on #602 / !564, which moves all versions into CI variables so that the regex managers can find them.

title: Update outdated tool versions in the CI pipeline
description:
## Summary

The versions of the tools used by the chart's CI pipeline are pinned by hand in `.gitlab-ci.yml` and have not been updated since !421 (August 2023). Several of them are end-of-life, and the kubectl download URL no longer serves current releases.

| Dependency | Pinned today | Current | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| CI base image | `gitlab-build-images:gitlab-charts-build-base-helm-3.7` | – | Helm 3.7 (2021); the newest Helm-only image in that repository is `helm-3.9` |
| `helm-unittest` | 0.3.4 | 1.2.1 | |
| `kind` | v0.20.0 | v0.33.0 | |
| `kubectl` | v1.27.4 | v1.37.1 | Kubernetes 1.27 is EOL; `storage.googleapis.com/kubernetes-release` returns 404 for recent versions, `dl.k8s.io` has to be used |
| `docker` / `docker:dind` | 20.10.16 | 29.9.2 | EOL; `-git` image variants are no longer published (the last one is 25.0.5) |
| `alpine` (release stable job) | 3.18 | 3.24 | 3.18 is EOL since May 2025 |
| Helm in integration tests | `get-helm-3 \| bash` (unpinned, "latest") | – | Now resolves to Helm 4, a different major than the lint/unit jobs use |

## Proposal

Bump all versions in one MR and keep every version as a `variables:` entry in `.gitlab-ci.yml`, adding `DOCKER_VERSION` and `HELM_VERSION`:

- switch the base image to `alpine/helm:${HELM_VERSION}`, because `gitlab-build-images` has no current Helm-only image;
- pin the Helm version used by the integration test to the same `HELM_VERSION`;
- download `kubectl` from `dl.k8s.io`;
- use `docker:${DOCKER_VERSION}-cli` for the integration job (`git` is not needed there).

`helm lint` and `helm unittest` (89 tests) pass locally with Helm 3.22.1 and helm-unittest 1.2.1.

Keeping these versions current automatically is a separate follow-up (Renovate bot onboarding).

title: Support dnsPolicy and dnsConfig for the runner manager pod
description:
## Problem

The chart has no way to set `dnsPolicy` or `dnsConfig` on the runner manager Deployment. With the Kubernetes default `ndots:5`, every lookup of a name with fewer than 5 dots walks the pod search list first. For the manager's job polling that means each `gitlab.com` lookup costs 10 DNS queries (A and AAAA for 4 search domains, then the name itself), 8 of them NXDOMAIN.

On our EKS clusters runner managers send about 1.3M DNS queries a day this way. Build pods can already be tuned through `[runners.kubernetes.dns_config]`, but the manager pod cannot.

## Proposal

Add two optional values, passed through to the manager pod spec as-is:

    dnsPolicy: ""
    dnsConfig: {}
    # e.g.
    # dnsConfig:
    #   options:
    #     - name: ndots
    #       value: "1"

This follows the existing pass-through values such as `hostAliases`, `priorityClassName` and `topologySpreadConstraints`.

## Workaround

Setting `gitlabUrl` to a fully qualified name with a trailing dot (`https://gitlab.com./`) avoids the search list for job polling. Other lookups made by the manager, such as the AWS STS endpoint for IRSA credentials, still walk the full search list.

title: Support Custom Labels on Auto-Generated Secrets and ConfigMaps for GitLab Kubernetes Runner Helm Chart:
description:
## Description:
When using the GitLab Kubernetes Runner Helm chart, two resource types are created without support for user-defined labels:  

1. Runner ConfigMap — A single ConfigMap is generated containing the runner configuration (concurrency, limits, etc.). There is currently no mechanism in the Helm chart to apply custom labels to this ConfigMap.

2. Job Secrets — For each CI/CD job, Kubernetes secrets (e.g., kubernetes.io/dockercfg type) are auto-generated with dynamically constructed names based on the job. Because the names are dynamic and no labels are applied at creation time, there is no reliable way to select or manage these secrets using label selectors after the fact.

## Requested behavior: 
Expose a Helm values option (e.g., runners.secret.labels and runners.configMap.labels) that allows users to define custom labels to be applied to both the runner ConfigMap and all job-spawned secrets. Alternatively, adding a common label that can be applied to the different pod generated elements.

## Impact: 
Without this capability, organizations with compliance or namespace governance requirements — such as those requiring label-based RBAC, cost allocation, or network policy enforcement — are forced to fork and maintain a custom version of the Helm chart, creating significant operational overhead.

title: Make image reference in values.yaml renovate-compatible
description:
Currently, the image reference in the orbit Chart's values.yaml file looks as follows:

```yaml
image:
  registry: registry.gitlab.com
  image: orbit/orbit
  # tag: alpine-v{{.Chart.AppVersion}}
```

Unfortunately, this is not compatible with the [Renovate helm-values manager](https://docs.renovatebot.com/modules/manager/helm-values/). This manager requires the following format:

```yaml
image:
  repository: 'some-docker/dependency'
  tag: v1.0.0
  registry: registry.example.com # optional key, will default to "docker.io"
```

Most Helm Charts follow this convention so it would be great if orbit could also use it. This would allow automated maintenance of the images used in the installed chart.

To avoid breaking changes and keep backward comaptibility, you could introduce `repository` as an alternative attribute name for `image`.

title: Automatic creation of runner configuration in a new workflow
description:
Hello!

In a new workflow, it seems that the «runner configuration» has to be created manually (at least I couldn’t find any instructions on how to automate this).

Am I correct in understanding that there’s only one process:

Create a new runner in the UI and obtain a token (either manually or via API).

Add it to values or a secret.

Is there any plan to automate this process, similar to how it was done with runnerRegistrationToken? I’d really prefer not to build a custom solution that would automate the entire process.

title: Add option to insert annotations to ConfigMaps
description:
Hello!

It would be nice to be able to insert annotations into configmaps.

Currently, it is possible to add annotations to pods, deployments, and other items (`podAnnotations` and `deploymentAnnotations`), but not to configmaps.

Annotations in configmaps can be used when managing configurations via vault (in my case, it's a bank-vault secret webhook).
